subject: Clarifying DPA incident notice windows, subprocessor access, and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Karen Nguyen <karen.nguyen@starlighthealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@starlighthealth.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident notice timing + subprocessor access (DPA section 6)

Hi Laura,

We're kicking off procurement diligence and a security review ahead of our Q4 pilot. One of our legal team items is clarity on incident notification and evidence cooperation under the DPA (section 6). A couple of concrete asks so we can proceed to the security committee tomorrow: 

- What is Redwood's committed initial notification window for incidents that may affect Starlight Health data (we currently track 24 / 48 / 72 hour asks from vendors)?
- When can we expect a scoped statement of impact (approx. hours) and a follow-up with evidence availability (forensics snapshots, logs) for incidents requiring export under cross-border rules?
- Will Redwood allow a named Starlight liaison (forensic contact) to access a secure export of logs / snapshots, or does everything go through a custodian/escrow process only?

For context our procurement policy flags any vendor that cannot provide clear timelines and a path for subprocessor involvement. I've attached the DPA excerpt our counsel is referencing and highlighted the incident paragraph.

If you can confirm today it will save a full escalation to legal. Happy to jump on a quick call this afternoon.

Thanks,
Karen
Karen Nguyen
Head of Security Operations
Starlight Health

Attachment: starlight_dpa_excerpt.pdf (pdf, 45 KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karen Nguyen <karen.nguyen@starlighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident notice timing + subprocessor access (DPA section 6)

Karen —

Thanks for the clear note and the excerpt. Quick answers up front, then internal owners below:

- Initial notification: Redwood's standard commitment for customer-impacting incidents is an initial triage notice within 24 hours of detection for incidents that meet the DPA "material impact" threshold. For lower-severity anomalies we typically provide a next-business-day advisory.
- Scoped statement: We provide a scoped impact statement (affected systems, data classes, estimated user count) within 72 hours where feasible. If additional forensic work is required we allocate a 7-day window for a substantive evidence package (forensic snapshot + log export) depending on legal/export constraints.
- Subprocessor access & handoff: We generally route access through a Red-team custodian process. Named customer liaisons can be granted access to a secure export under an approved evidence-handshake (C2C transfer) or, when required by contract, via an escrow agent. For cross-border exports we work with legal to apply minimization and redaction and to provide only the necessary artifacts.

I've CC'd Marissa (legal ops lead) and Ben (privacy/forensic lead) to confirm any exceptions for regulated healthcare deployments.

If that aligns with Starlight's expectations we'd propose a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a one-hour run-through of the evidence-handover steps Monday morning.

Best,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracting, Americas
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dpa-excerpt-incident-section.pdf (pdf, 12 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: proposed MAP and compliance constraints for Starlight

Laura / team —

Following Karen's ask and your reply, I drafted a conservative MAP for approval. Please review and call out any non-negotiable constraints (we'll need to surface these to Starlight):

1) Initial notice: 24 hours for material incidents (detection timestamp) — communications team drafts customer notice, notify list: security/legal/customer success.
2) Scoped impact: 72 hours — includes high-level affected services, data classes (PHI/PII tag), estimated volume.
3) Evidence package: target 7 days for a secure forensic snapshot + structured logs. This may be extended if evidence contains cross-border data requiring export review.
4) Subprocessor access: we offer two paths:
   - Controlled export to an agreed custodian mailbox (preferred)
   - Direct access for named Starlight liaison under an earlier-signed Access Addendum + NDA, enforced via temporary credentials and audit hooks.
5) Escrow/third-party transfer: for customers that require an escrow we can coordinate with our recommended partners; this adds a standard 48–72 hour coordination window.

Notes / constraints:
- We cannot commit to arbitrary raw-dump exports; forensic exports are scoped and redacted where possible.
- Cross-border transfers will require legal sign-off and may introduce a delay beyond the 7-day target.
- If the incident implicates a Redwood subprocessor, we will coordinate subprocessor-specific evidence requests (subprocessor SLA varies).

Ben — can you attach the forensics-handover checklist and any standard Access Addendum text? Nikhil — please call out any required IR (incident response) SLAs we should not promise to customers.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: forensics-handover-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 18 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karen Nguyen <karen.nguyen@starlighthealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident notice timing + subprocessor access (DPA section 6)

Karen —

Appreciate the quick coordination. To confirm and make it operational for Starlight:

- We confirm the MAP Marissa outlined above (24h initial, 72h scoped, 7d evidence target).
- For healthcare customers, we will open an Incident Liaison channel and execute the Access Addendum before providing any direct liaison access. That typically takes one business day once signed.
- If escrow is preferred, please indicate your vendor of choice; otherwise we'll propose Redwood-trusted escrow partners and a single coordination lead.

Next steps:
- Laura, can you confirm contract language for the initial notice window (we'll add a short clause to the SOW appendix)?
- Karen, if Monday 09:00 PT works we'll do the one-hour run-through and sign the Access Addendum during the call.

I'll attach the checklist and a redline template for the Access Addendum in the Drive link Marissa included.

Thanks,
